topics.headline: Canada suspends trade talks with US as 50% tariffs take effect
topics.snippet: Canada suspended all trade negotiations with the Trump administration late in the evening and directed its negotiators to return to Ottawa, citing unfair economic terms brought into the talks. A 50% t…
topics.text:
canada suspends trade talks with us as 50% tariffs take effect
canada suspended all trade negotiations with the trump administration late in the evening and directed its negotiators to return to ottawa, citing unfair economic terms brought into the talks. a 50% tariff now applies to roughly $28 billion worth of canadian goods entering the united states, and canada has said it will match the measures dollar for dollar. the united states now has higher tariffs on most canadian goods than on goods from china. canada's statement said its government had recognised from the outset that america had changed and that the old relationship would not return.

topics.headline: Pentagon fires Stars and Stripes publisher, editor and Middle East reporter
topics.snippet: The Pentagon dismissed the publisher of Stars and Stripes, its editor, and Middle East reporter Laura Coat. Coat said the Department of Defense told her she was fired for insubordination after she tol…
topics.text:
pentagon fires stars and stripes publisher, editor and middle east reporter
the pentagon dismissed the publisher of stars and stripes, its editor, and middle east reporter laura coat. coat said the department of defense told her she was fired for insubordination after she told a cbs reporter that she works for stars and stripes rather than for the pentagon or any administration or policymaker. the paper, which is partly funded by the pentagon and partly from outside sources, had been reporting on how the conflict in iran has affected service members, on conditions they face overseas, and on military families' objections to defense secretary pete hegseth. earlier reporting had indicated the pentagon was weighing firing the longtime publisher ahead of his planned retirement.

topics.snippet: Pentagon data show 757 United States troops have been wounded in operations against Iran. The figure was released as part of official Defense Department reporting on the campaign.
topics.text:
pentagon says 757 us troops wounded in operations against iran
pentagon data show 757 united states troops have been wounded in operations against iran. the figure was released as part of official defense department reporting on the campaign.

topics.headline: Israel strikes Syrian airport as Turkey issues arrest warrant for Netanyahu
topics.snippet: Israel bombed an airport in Syria that a Turkish delegation had visited only hours before the strikes. Turkey subsequently issued an arrest warrant for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and Israeli o…
topics.text:
israel strikes syrian airport as turkey issues arrest warrant for netanyahu
israel bombed an airport in syria that a turkish delegation had visited only hours before the strikes. turkey subsequently issued an arrest warrant for prime minister benjamin netanyahu, and israeli officials responded by accusing turkish president recep tayyip erdogan of antisemitism. because turkey is a nato member, an escalation to open conflict raises the question of whether article 5 could be invoked and how the united states would respond given its separate relationship with israel.

topics.headline: American detained three hours by DHS over tweet criticising Israeli minister
topics.snippet: A US citizen returning from a trip to Lebanon said Department of Homeland Security agents took his passport at the passport line and questioned him for three hours about Israel. He said agents asked a…
topics.text:
american detained three hours by dhs over tweet criticising israeli minister
a us citizen returning from a trip to lebanon said department of homeland security agents took his passport at the passport line and questioned him for three hours about israel. he said agents asked about his family, friends and schooling, searched his social media accounts, and focused on a tweet he posted in april 2026 criticising israeli minister itamar ben-gvir, telling him not to do it again. he said agents recorded his phone number, email and address before releasing him, and he described the episode as his own government questioning him on behalf of a foreign one. he cited ben-gvir's statements about passing a death penalty law for palestinians, building an execution facility, and setting nightly casualty targets for israeli forces in gaza.

topics.headline: Supreme Court chief justice lets Trump's $400M White House ballroom construction proceed
topics.snippet: Chief Justice John Roberts issued an unsigned order staying a lower court's preliminary injunction that would have halted construction of President Trump's $400 million White House ballroom. The order…
topics.text:
supreme court chief justice lets trump's $400m white house ballroom construction proceed
chief justice john roberts issued an unsigned order staying a lower court's preliminary injunction that would have halted construction of president trump's $400 million white house ballroom. the order allows work to continue pending further action by the supreme court. the court has not indicated when or whether it will rule on the underlying case.

topics.headline: ICE body camera footage shows agents using racial slurs during Los Angeles operations
topics.snippet: Video obtained by the ACLU through a lawsuit alleging racial discrimination shows Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents using racial slurs while conducting immigration enforcement in Los Angeles.…
topics.text:
ice body camera footage shows agents using racial slurs during los angeles operations
video obtained by the aclu through a lawsuit alleging racial discrimination shows immigration and customs enforcement agents using racial slurs while conducting immigration enforcement in los angeles. the footage came from an agent's body camera. ice characterised the language as "operational shorthand."

topics.headline: Trump to import foreign beef and cap prices as ranchers object
topics.snippet: President Trump said he will import hundreds of thousands of pounds of beef into the United States and impose a price cap, as domestic supply tightens and beef prices rise. He has not disclosed which…
topics.text:
trump to import foreign beef and cap prices as ranchers object
president trump said he will import hundreds of thousands of pounds of beef into the united states and impose a price cap, as domestic supply tightens and beef prices rise. he has not disclosed which countries the imported beef will come from. ranchers who support the administration objected, saying domestic beef should be used instead, and raised concerns about the food safety standards of unnamed suppliers. tariffs have been cited as a factor in the higher domestic prices.

topics.headline: Trump suggests military intervention over bond market and claims Strait of Hormuz as US territory
topics.snippet: President Trump suggested he may use military intervention to stabilise the bond market. He also said he now considers the Strait of Hormuz to be United States territory, prompting objections from sev…
topics.text:
trump suggests military intervention over bond market and claims strait of hormuz as us territory
president trump suggested he may use military intervention to stabilise the bond market. he also said he now considers the strait of hormuz to be united states territory, prompting objections from several middle eastern countries whose territory the claim implicates.

topics.headline: Utah governor defends monument shrinkage as advocates say it only enables mining
topics.snippet: Utah Governor Spencer Cox defended the decision to shrink Grand Staircase-Escalante and Bears Ears national monuments, saying polling showing Utahns oppose it changes once respondents are asked whethe…
topics.text:
utah governor defends monument shrinkage as advocates say it only enables mining
utah governor spencer cox defended the decision to shrink grand staircase-escalante and bears ears national monuments, saying polling showing utahns oppose it changes once respondents are asked whether they support what shrinking actually does, and that residents want more local, state and county input and continued access. public lands advocates responded that hiking, camping, hunting and grazing were always permitted inside the monuments, so the only activity monument status blocked was mining and drilling. they noted presidents have used the antiquities act 168 times and that about half of us national parks, including zion, acadia, olympic and the grand canyon, began as national monuments. cox has said he wants utah to become the top destination for critical mineral extraction and processing.

topics.headline: Bureau of Land Management sent thousands of wild horses to slaughter in 2025
topics.snippet: The New York Times reported that roughly 3,700 wild horses were sent to slaughter in 2025 under the Bureau of Land Management. Slaughtering wild horses is illegal in the United States, but the agency…
topics.text:
bureau of land management sent thousands of wild horses to slaughter in 2025
the new york times reported that roughly 3,700 wild horses were sent to slaughter in 2025 under the bureau of land management. slaughtering wild horses is illegal in the united states, but the agency is using a legal loophole to round up mustangs and sell them to buyers including a slaughterhouse in ohio, from where the animals may be trucked overseas for processing. critics say the roundups use helicopters to drive herds, including foals, into capture pens, and that animals are sold for as little as $25 a head. the practice was previously rare.

topics.snippet: The Department of Defense faces a $285 billion maintenance backlog across its facilities. Troops are contending with mold, excessive heat and aging base infrastructure as a result.
topics.text:

topics.headline: Israeli think tank to lobby Congress for $40 billion over ten years
topics.snippet: The Jewish Institute for National Security of America is preparing to lobby members of Congress for $40 billion per year over the next ten years as a base minimum in US support. The organisation's pro…
topics.text:
israeli think tank to lobby congress for $40 billion over ten years
the jewish institute for national security of america is preparing to lobby members of congress for $40 billion per year over the next ten years as a base minimum in us support. the organisation's proposal also asks that israel be designated a "model ally" rather than described as america's "greatest ally." the proposal is not public policy.

topics.headline: New Jersey budget expands food aid, Medicaid backfill and property tax relief
topics.snippet: New Jersey passed a budget under Governor Mikie Sherrill that invests $71 million in SNAP and other food assistance to offset federal cuts, and $34.6 billion to replace lost Medicaid funding. The budg…
topics.text:
new jersey budget expands food aid, medicaid backfill and property tax relief
new jersey passed a budget under governor mikie sherrill that invests $71 million in snap and other food assistance to offset federal cuts, and $34.6 billion to replace lost medicaid funding. the budget includes what is described as the largest property tax relief package in state history, a substantial increase in the child tax credit, and expanded down payment assistance for home buyers. it also allocates $1.1 billion to new jersey transit, $234 million more than the previous year, and cuts the state deficit in half.

topics.headline: FDA says recalled Taylor Farms lettuce reached nine more states and territories
topics.snippet: The Food and Drug Administration now says recalled shredded lettuce from a Taylor Farms facility in Mexico may have reached nine additional states and territories, including California, Delaware, Nort…
topics.text:
fda says recalled taylor farms lettuce reached nine more states and territories
the food and drug administration now says recalled shredded lettuce from a taylor farms facility in mexico may have reached nine additional states and territories, including california, delaware, north dakota, rhode island, south dakota, vermont, washington, puerto rico and the district of columbia. the product is linked to the largest cyclospora outbreak recorded in the united states, with more than 10,000 illnesses reported across 17 states. the outbreak is ongoing and the case count may rise given the newly disclosed distribution. a separate recall of alfalfa sprouts was also announced.

topics.headline: Official IDF account appears on American TikTok
topics.snippet: A verified official Israel Defense Forces account has appeared on the American version of TikTok. The account's presence on the platform drew attention as an instance of a foreign military operating a…
topics.text:
official idf account appears on american tiktok
a verified official israel defense forces account has appeared on the american version of tiktok. the account's presence on the platform drew attention as an instance of a foreign military operating a verified profile aimed at us users.

topics.headline: Forecasters expect strongest El Nino on record
topics.snippet: This year's El Nino is projected to be the strongest observed in living memory. The forecast was included among the day's developments without further detail on expected regional impacts.

topics.headline: Judge recommends Epstein survivors' negligence suit against FBI proceed
topics.snippet: A federal magistrate judge has recommended that a lawsuit brought by more than 30 Epstein survivors against the FBI and the Department of Justice be allowed to move forward. The suit alleges the FBI w…
topics.text:
judge recommends epstein survivors' negligence suit against fbi proceed
a federal magistrate judge has recommended that a lawsuit brought by more than 30 epstein survivors against the fbi and the department of justice be allowed to move forward. the suit alleges the fbi was negligent in failing to act on credible tips, including a report made by maria farmer in 1996, and argues that acting on those tips would have prevented further abuse. the recommendation now goes to the district court, which will decide whether the case proceeds. many of the plaintiffs remain anonymous as jane does.

topics.headline: Hegseth brings wife into sensitive Pentagon meetings, report says
topics.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has brought his wife, Jennifer Hegseth, into sensitive military meetings, according to a New York Times report, alarming national security officials. She is described as…
topics.text:
hegseth brings wife into sensitive pentagon meetings, report says
defense secretary pete hegseth has brought his wife, jennifer hegseth, into sensitive military meetings, according to a new york times report, alarming national security officials. she is described as his de facto most influential adviser at the pentagon and has accompanied him on travel, with hegseth saying he wants her present to "keep him out of trouble" amid a history of heavy drinking. she was also reported to be the primary force behind removing most institutional journalists from the pentagon press corps.

topics.headline: Navy weighs renaming USS Doris Miller after Trump
topics.snippet: The U.S. Navy is discussing removing the name of Doris Miller from an aircraft carrier under construction and renaming it after Donald Trump, according to CNN reporting. Miller was a Black sailor who…
topics.text:
navy weighs renaming uss doris miller after trump
the u.s. navy is discussing removing the name of doris miller from an aircraft carrier under construction and renaming it after donald trump, according to cnn reporting. miller was a black sailor who fought during japan's attack on pearl harbor, and the navy is considering naming another warship for him and recommending him for the medal of honor. no aircraft carrier has previously been named for a sitting president.

topics.headline: Leaked letters from White House aide Natalie Harp to Trump draw scrutiny
topics.snippet: Two letters written by 35-year-old White House aide Natalie Harp to Donald Trump have been leaked, the first obtained by the Daily Beast. The letters are personal in tone, apologising for being left b…
topics.text:
leaked letters from white house aide natalie harp to trump draw scrutiny
two letters written by 35-year-old white house aide natalie harp to donald trump have been leaked, the first obtained by the daily beast. the letters are personal in tone, apologising for being left behind on a trip and thanking trump as her "guardian and protector in life." harp reportedly declined to complete forms for a security clearance during her first year at the white house and serves as an intermediary for foreign leaders seeking to communicate with the president, raising national security questions.

topics.headline: Reported leak of FBI notes said to implicate Trump in Epstein case

topics.text:
reported leak of fbi notes said to implicate trump in epstein case
more than half of the fbi notes said to have been withheld by the department of justice have reportedly been leaked online, posted to reddit. the notes are claimed to reference donald trump and other powerful figures in connection with jeffrey epstein. the department of justice is accused of concealing the material.

topics.headline: Midterm elections set for November 3 with guidance on registration and state rules
topics.snippet: The U.S. midterm elections will be held on November 3. Voters are advised to check their registration, since purges and roll maintenance often occur quietly in off years, and to confirm state deadline…
topics.text:
midterm elections set for november 3 with guidance on registration and state rules
the u.s. midterm elections will be held on november 3. voters are advised to check their registration, since purges and roll maintenance often occur quietly in off years, and to confirm state deadlines, which range from same-day registration to 30 days out and differ on whether mail ballots are counted by postmark or by receipt. in utah, ballots must reach the county clerk by 8 p.m. on election night, postmarks no longer count, and voters must write the last four digits of their utah id or social security number on the return envelope; automatic mail ballots phase out by 2029. election rules are set by states and congress under article i, section 4, and federal courts have twice struck down presidential attempts to set them.

topics.headline: Trump plans election monitors as Musk pledges midterm spending

topics.text:
trump plans election monitors as musk pledges midterm spending
donald trump is sending more than a thousand election monitors to oversee precincts across the country ahead of the midterms. elon musk plans to spend more than $200 million on the midterm elections. the trump administration is also seeking to prosecute a teacher running against senator dan sullivan in alaska, who shares the senator's name.

topics.headline: Northwest Indiana residents enter tenth day without power
topics.snippet: Tens of thousands of residents in Northwest Indiana have been without electricity for more than nine days following deadly storms on August 11, with more than 20,000 people affected in Gary alone. Res…
topics.text:
northwest indiana residents enter tenth day without power
tens of thousands of residents in northwest indiana have been without electricity for more than nine days following deadly storms on august 11, with more than 20,000 people affected in gary alone. residents are using social media to locate working laundromats, wifi, food, diapers and cleaning supplies, and are queuing for hot meals and places to charge phones.

topics.headline: Calls mount for RFK Jr. to resign as foodborne illness cases rise
topics.snippet: Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is facing growing calls to resign amid anger over the state of the U.S. public health system. Foodborne illnesses have risen sharply this year…
topics.text:
calls mount for rfk jr. to resign as foodborne illness cases rise
health and human services secretary robert f. kennedy jr. is facing growing calls to resign amid anger over the state of the u.s. public health system. foodborne illnesses have risen sharply this year, attributed in part to cuts made under his leadership, though the overall number of recalls is not significantly higher than last year. recent incidents include an fda recall of sourdough bread sold in washington state over possible metal shard contamination, a salmonella outbreak linked to jalapenos that has infected 431 people across 32 states, a recall of nearly 40,000 bottles of eyedrops over possible metal contamination, and an unusual alfalfa sprout outbreak in minnesota and wisconsin involving both e. coli and salmonella that has sickened at least 23 people and hospitalised two.

researchers flag 152 wallets over $8m in military-event bets
researchers have flagged 152 unusually successful wallets that placed roughly $8 million in bets on military events on the prediction market polymarket. the pattern has raised questions about possible insider trading around defence and security outcomes.

lending apps including afterpay, klarna and intuit are now offering buy-now-pay-later options for electricity bills, insurance, dentist visits, rent and physicals. the expansion moves short-term consumer credit into essential household spending.

topics.snippet: OpenAI has launched an Apple Messages integration for ChatGPT on Mac, allowing the chatbot to access a user's full message history and send texts on their behalf. The feature lets ChatGPT read, write…

chatgpt gains access to apple messages on mac
openai has launched an apple messages integration for chatgpt on mac, allowing the chatbot to access a user's full message history and send texts on their behalf. the feature lets chatgpt read, write and send messages, as well as summarise conversations and extract information from them.

topics.headline: Trump administration has lost all 21 election-law cases in federal court
topics.snippet: Democracy Forward president Skye Perryman said the administration is 0 for 21 in cases involving voter data and federal attempts to intervene in elections, with rulings against it including from judge…
topics.text:
trump administration has lost all 21 election-law cases in federal court
democracy forward president skye perryman said the administration is 0 for 21 in cases involving voter data and federal attempts to intervene in elections, with rulings against it including from judges appointed by republican presidents. perryman said courts have blocked the use of a modified save database and that discovery is being pursued to establish what the administration is doing before election day. perryman said the constitution grants the president no authority over elections, and that lawyers are prepared to challenge any attempt to prevent votes from being cast or counted.

topics.headline: Air Force major detained after calling for Trump's impeachment over Iran war
topics.snippet: Major Jason Watson, described as the first active-duty service member to call for the impeachment and removal of the president and vice president over the war in Iran, has been ordered into pretrial c…
topics.text:
air force major detained after calling for trump's impeachment over iran war
major jason watson, described as the first active-duty service member to call for the impeachment and removal of the president and vice president over the war in iran, has been ordered into pretrial confinement, according to cnn. watson appeared outside the us capitol in uniform and later said on cnn that trump was flagrantly violating the constitution, breaking the law, engaging in corruption and killing americans, adding he was willing to pay the highest price for speaking out. the uniform code of military justice criminalizes contemptuous words directed at the president and other senior officials, and public dissent by active-duty members is rare.

topics.headline: Trump announces sweeping economic campaign against Iran and threatens third countries
topics.snippet: Trump announced what he called the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country, describing it as economic warfare and isolation against Iran on an unprecedented scale and saying Ir…
topics.text:
trump announces sweeping economic campaign against iran and threatens third countries
trump announced what he called the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country, describing it as economic warfare and isolation against iran on an unprecedented scale and saying iran's navy, air force and military factories have been destroyed. he warned that any country whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or government entities provide a lifeline to iran will face economic consequences, naming oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries and front companies. separately, the united arab emirates suspended trade and financial ties with iran following a new missile threat.

topics.headline: Trump states North Korea has 57 nuclear weapons as Pyongyang launches missiles
topics.snippet: Trump said publicly that Kim Jong-un has 57 nuclear weapons and that he will meet the North Korean leader by the end of the year, remarks characterized as disclosing likely classified information; Sou…
topics.text:
trump states north korea has 57 nuclear weapons as pyongyang launches missiles
trump said publicly that kim jong-un has 57 nuclear weapons and that he will meet the north korean leader by the end of the year, remarks characterized as disclosing likely classified information; south korea puts the figure closer to 80 to 120, according to cbs. trump also suggested south korea should be penalized for not joining the war in iran, and pulled back from joint military drills. north korea responded overnight by launching roughly 10 ballistic missiles, and kim's sister said she was unaware of any communication between the two leaders and that pyongyang's posture toward the united states is unchanged.

topics.headline: White House aide Natalie Harp worked a year without a security clearance
topics.snippet: Reporting says Natalie Harp worked at the White House for more than a year while repeatedly declining to complete routine security clearance paperwork, and is only now in the process of obtaining one,…
topics.text:
white house aide natalie harp worked a year without a security clearance
reporting says natalie harp worked at the white house for more than a year while repeatedly declining to complete routine security clearance paperwork, and is only now in the process of obtaining one, despite close proximity to the president and likely access to highly classified information. maggie haberman reported that harp served as a channel through which foreign leaders sought to reach the president. the white house is now searching for the source of the leaks, since the lack of a clearance was known only internally, and the story has displaced the administration's agenda with under 80 days until november's elections.

topics.headline: Disney and ABC sue FCC as Republicans criticize Brendan Carr
topics.snippet: ABC and Disney have filed a First Amendment lawsuit against the FCC and chairman Brendan Carr alleging retaliation, amid growing Republican criticism from figures including Tom DeLay and Senator John…
topics.text:
disney and abc sue fcc as republicans criticize brendan carr
abc and disney have filed a first amendment lawsuit against the fcc and chairman brendan carr alleging retaliation, amid growing republican criticism from figures including tom delay and senator john kennedy. twenty-one conservative groups sent carr a letter warning that license renewal should not become a tool for influencing lawful negotiations, and commentators noted carr's 2019 statement that the fcc must stop micromanaging local broadcasters' business operations. carr pushed through a party-line vote eliminating the fcc's 39% ownership cap, trump has nominated a staff attorney to an open commission seat, and the fcc is intervening in negotiations between local stations and the big four networks.

topics.headline: US national debt passes $40 trillion as Treasury doubles buyback operations

topics.text:
us national debt passes $40 trillion as treasury doubles buyback operations
the united states has reached $40 trillion in national debt, and treasury secretary scott bessent said the government will double its operations buying back its own 10- to 30-year securities. the buyback expansion was characterized as a response to weak foreign demand for us debt. several major hedge funds are reported to be shorting us markets.

israel opens criminal probes into killings of hind rajab and gaza aid workers
israel has opened criminal investigations into the killings of hind rajab and 15 emergency and aid workers in gaza. the investigations are being conducted by the military.

israel building execution facility overseen by ben-gvir
israel is constructing gallows intended for people it designates as terrorists, in a project overseen by national security minister itamar ben-gvir. the plans include a front-row viewing area for the families of those executed. the project was discussed in the knesset in march of this year and required sign-off from multiple officials.

topics.text:

forest service moves to rescind the roadless rule entirely
agriculture secretary brooke rollins announced on august 18 that the us forest service has filed a proposed rule to fully rescind the 2001 roadless area conservation rule. the rule barred new road construction, reconstruction, and commercial logging across 58.5 million acres of inventoried roadless areas, and was backed by 90 percent of 1.6 million public comments when adopted. the rescission would open 44.7 million acres across 39 states to road building and industrial logging, at a time when the agency's road maintenance backlog stands at $11.2 billion. the affected areas include habitat for wildlife and drinking water sources for 25 million americans; a pew poll found 76 percent of american voters, including 76 percent of trump voters, support keeping the rule.

topics.snippet: Senators Rand Paul and Ron Johnson are reviewing 34,000 text messages, 522 voicemails and emails released from Anthony Fauci. One May 27, 2021 email from then-FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock told Fauc…
topics.text:
released fauci emails show fda official raised vaccine adverse event concerns
senators rand paul and ron johnson are reviewing 34,000 text messages, 522 voicemails and emails released from anthony fauci. one may 27, 2021 email from then-fda commissioner janet woodcock told fauci she had been contacted by a number of people, many of them healthcare professionals, reporting adverse events after covid-19 vaccination from all three available vaccines, and that no one was taking them seriously or studying the reports. fauci forwarded the message saying "we cannot ignore her" and suggested bringing in the cdc.

topics.text:
nationwide recall of outshine frozen fruit bars over glass contamination
dreyer's grand ice cream is voluntarily recalling a large quantity of outshine frozen fruit bars sold nationwide due to possible glass contamination. the recall covers select lots of strawberry, watermelon, grape, tangerine and black cherry six-count 2.5-ounce bars, with expiration dates in 2027. no other outshine products are affected, and affected batch numbers are listed on the fda's website.

actress hayden panettiere died at age 36. the official report attributes the death to an overdose and states that no foul play was involved. three months earlier she had described on a podcast being sexually abused by powerful figures in hollywood.

topics.headline: Trump orders joint military exercises with South Korea scaled back

topics.text:
trump orders joint military exercises with south korea scaled back
donald trump announced he has instructed secretary of war pete hegseth to substantially reduce the joint military exercises the united states has conducted with south korea, citing his "very good relationship" with north korean leader kim jong un and calling the drills costly and a hostile signal. trump also said he had asked the south korean president to join the united states in what he termed the denuclearization of the islamic republic of iran, and that south korea declined. the exercises have been held in some form since the 1970s, and north korea has long objected to them.

topics.headline: Marjorie Taylor Greene says nuclear weapons are being discussed in Iran strategy meetings
topics.snippet: Former Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene said that the use of nuclear weapons against Iran is being discussed in top military strategy meetings, stating she was not speculating and calling the disc…
topics.text:
marjorie taylor greene says nuclear weapons are being discussed in iran strategy meetings
former congresswoman marjorie taylor greene said that the use of nuclear weapons against iran is being discussed in top military strategy meetings, stating she was not speculating and calling the discussions "pure evil." her post drew comparisons to the 1945 bombings of hiroshima and nagasaki, the last time nuclear weapons were used in war. the claim has not been confirmed by the administration or the pentagon.

topics.headline: Trump threatens to bomb Oman over Iran negotiations
topics.snippet: Speaking with a Fox News host, Donald Trump said he would "bomb the shit out of" Oman if it got in the way of a deal with Iran. Oman is a longstanding US ally in the Gulf and has repeatedly acted as a…
topics.text:
trump threatens to bomb oman over iran negotiations
speaking with a fox news host, donald trump said he would "bomb the shit out of" oman if it got in the way of a deal with iran. oman is a longstanding us ally in the gulf and has repeatedly acted as an intermediary in communications between washington and tehran. there is no current indication oman is obstructing talks, and the roughly 60-day window trump had set for reaching an agreement is nearing its end without a deal.

topics.headline: Supreme Court denies Trump rehearing in E. Jean Carroll case
topics.snippet: The Supreme Court issued an unsigned order denying Donald Trump's request for a rehearing in his appeal of the E. Jean Carroll case, in which a jury found him liable for sexual assault and he has alre…
topics.text:
supreme court denies trump rehearing in e. jean carroll case
the supreme court issued an unsigned order denying donald trump's request for a rehearing in his appeal of the e. jean carroll case, in which a jury found him liable for sexual assault and he has already paid more than $5 million. the court had rejected his initial appeal about a month earlier, and rehearing requests are rarely granted. no justice was recorded as dissenting, and the case is now concluded.

topics.headline: Attorney General Todd Blanche says he will not pledge independence from the White House
topics.snippet: Attorney General Todd Blanche, who previously served as Donald Trump's personal criminal defense lawyer, said in an interview with Kristen Welker that he would not pledge to be independent of the Whit…
topics.text:
attorney general todd blanche says he will not pledge independence from the white house
attorney general todd blanche, who previously served as donald trump's personal criminal defense lawyer, said in an interview with kristen welker that he would not pledge to be independent of the white house, calling the suggestion that the two are separate ludicrous. the statement breaks with decades of precedent treating the justice department as insulated from direct presidential control.

topics.headline: Majority of US voters say they are worse off financially under Trump
topics.snippet: A Focal Data poll for the Financial Times found that 53 percent of registered voters say they feel worse off financially than they did under Joe Biden, the first time a majority has said so since Trum…
topics.text:
majority of us voters say they are worse off financially under trump
a focal data poll for the financial times found that 53 percent of registered voters say they feel worse off financially than they did under joe biden, the first time a majority has said so since trump took office. among independents the figure is 57 percent, and nearly a quarter of republicans also say they are worse off. two-thirds of those polled said the economy is heading in the wrong direction, against 25 percent who said it is on the right track.

ukraine launches one of the largest drone strikes of the war on russia
ukraine struck russia's largest wildberries distribution facility, located roughly 30 kilometres south of moscow, in what is described as one of the biggest drone attacks of the war. the damage is estimated to run into billions of dollars, and six civilians are reported to have been killed.

topics.headline: Messages scrawled on US military aircraft in the Gulf point to low troop morale

topics.text:
messages scrawled on us military aircraft in the gulf point to low troop morale
photographs said to have been sent from us servicemen stationed in the persian gulf show writing on the wing flap of an air force kc-135r stratotanker, including phrases such as "operation epstein theory" and "peace deal #64 incoming" alongside remarks about israel. trita parsi, executive vice president of the quincy institute, said the images were sent to him from the field. the messages are being read as an indication of low morale among deployed personnel.

topics.headline: Trump attacks BBC over subpoenas of his family
topics.snippet: Donald Trump's legal team accused the BBC of abusing the deposition process after the broadcaster sought to subpoena Donald Trump Jr., Ivanka Trump and other family members. The BBC is seeking testimo…
topics.text:
trump attacks bbc over subpoenas of his family
donald trump's legal team accused the bbc of abusing the deposition process after the broadcaster sought to subpoena donald trump jr., ivanka trump and other family members. the bbc is seeking testimony about the president's state of mind around january 6, 2021, as part of its defence against trump's $10 billion defamation suit. in a statement to the telegraph, trump's lawyers said the bbc was harassing him and his family to distract from its own liability.

topics.headline: Melania Trump absent from public events amid possible Epstein-related inquiry

topics.text:
melania trump absent from public events amid possible epstein-related inquiry
the first lady has not appeared alongside donald trump for several weeks and has skipped high-profile washington events, including lindsey graham's funeral, while her instagram account has been dormant for more than two weeks. representative robert garcia has said she is near the top of the list of figures democrats would investigate over the epstein matter if the party takes control of the house. her public schedule during the second term has been substantially lighter than that of recent first ladies.

topics.headline: Campaign launches Pro-Human AI Declaration seeking a million signatures

topics.text:
campaign launches pro-human ai declaration seeking a million signatures
a coalition operating under the name stop the race to replace has published a pro-human ai declaration and is seeking one million signatures in support of regulating artificial intelligence. backers argue that while ai has beneficial applications in medical research, environmental monitoring and accessibility, it is increasingly being used to displace human creators, therapists and companions. the declaration's central claim is that ai should adapt to humanity rather than the reverse.

nationwide recalls issued over salmonella and listeria contamination
hampton grocer inc. is recalling eight-ounce packages of its lactnola lactation granola, sold on amazon between october 21, 2025 and august 12, 2026, after an ingredient tested positive for salmonella. walmart is separately recalling about 3,000 marketside 14-ounce tomato bisque soup kits sold in more than 29 states over possible listeria contamination, with upc 194346474004 and an expiration date of august 22, 2026. the recalls come amid a reported 400 percent surge in foodborne illness in the united states.

topics.text:
ossoff criticises trump's conduct as troops deploy in iran war
senator jon ossoff publicly criticised donald trump's handling of the war, saying that while sailors aboard the uss lincoln fight, the president sleeps through meetings, golfs and trades stocks. ossoff also referenced trump's focus on his ballroom project and his travel with close aide natalie harp. the remarks bring congressional attention to the president's relationship with harp, a longtime aide.

gulf allies weigh ending us base hosting over iran war strategy
washington post reporting indicates saudi arabia, the united arab emirates, qatar, kuwait and bahrain have lost confidence in the trump administration's handling of the war in iran. some of those governments have begun to debate the utility of continuing to host large us military installations on their territory. the states are described as united in frustration over the administration's failure to deliver the diplomacy needed to end the conflict and secure a lasting regional settlement.

topics.text:
trump signals a 2028 run as aides brace for investigations
the president posted "trump 2028" material on truth social, renewing questions about whether he intends to seek another term. separately, white house officials told cnn they expect a difficult next two years, citing expanding investigations into the president and his family, anticipated subpoenas and the possibility of impeachment. officials say he privately does not see a path to holding congress, and has only now begun spending hundreds of millions in campaign funds and appearing at rallies.

topics.headline: Defense Department to teach Christianity in military schools

topics.text:
defense department to teach christianity in military schools
according to the associated press, the department of defense will begin teaching christian content in the schools it operates for military families this fall. the department runs roughly 160 k-12 schools serving about 70,000 students. the course is titled "western civilization" and uses a text described as a history of the western tradition covering the ancient world and christendom.

topics.headline: FDA raises egg recall to its highest risk classification
topics.snippet: The FDA has elevated a recall covering more than a million dozen eggs to Class I, its most serious level, meaning consumption could cause severe illness or death. The eggs came from Midwest Poultry Se…
topics.text:
fda raises egg recall to its highest risk classification
the fda has elevated a recall covering more than a million dozen eggs to class i, its most serious level, meaning consumption could cause severe illness or death. the eggs came from midwest poultry services farms in texas and were distributed in the south and southwest with sell-by dates through august 17. dozens of people have been infected with salmonella and some hospitalized, amid a reported sharp rise in foodborne illness over the past year.

topics.headline: US home buyers fall to lowest level since 2013
topics.snippet: Redfin data show about 967,000 home buyers in the market in July, the fewest of any month since 2013. Rising housing costs and limited inventory are cited as the principal causes. The figure lands ami…
topics.text:
us home buyers fall to lowest level since 2013
redfin data show about 967,000 home buyers in the market in july, the fewest of any month since 2013. rising housing costs and limited inventory are cited as the principal causes. the figure lands amid broader concerns about affordability for younger buyers.

topics.headline: Sailors aboard USS Boxer report shortages of hygiene supplies
topics.snippet: A family member of a crew member aboard the USS Boxer reports that women on the ship have run out of feminine hygiene products because resupply and port calls have not occurred during repeated deploym…
topics.text:
sailors aboard uss boxer report shortages of hygiene supplies
a family member of a crew member aboard the uss boxer reports that women on the ship have run out of feminine hygiene products because resupply and port calls have not occurred during repeated deployment extensions. care packages sent by families are reportedly not being delivered. the account follows similar reports from other deployed vessels during the conflict.

topics.headline: Record Arctic Reserve lease sale sets up fight over further drilling
topics.snippet: Leases in the Western Arctic reserve sold in March for a record $163.7 million, and four additional lease sales are required by law over the next decade. The area supports hundreds of thousands of mol…
topics.text:
record arctic reserve lease sale sets up fight over further drilling
leases in the western arctic reserve sold in march for a record $163.7 million, and four additional lease sales are required by law over the next decade. the area supports hundreds of thousands of molting geese that are flightless for weeks each summer, nesting shorebirds that disperse across the hemisphere, and caribou calving grounds. opponents of development argue the absence of roads and infrastructure is precisely what makes the habitat function.

topics.headline: Kentucky district used AI to generate middle school curriculum
topics.snippet: A school in Jefferson County, Kentucky produced much of its middle school curriculum using AI, and parents have objected to widespread errors in the materials. A distributed map rendered state names a…
topics.text:
kentucky district used ai to generate middle school curriculum
a school in jefferson county, kentucky produced much of its middle school curriculum using ai, and parents have objected to widespread errors in the materials. a distributed map rendered state names as "new mizzone," "veneque" and "south cilantro," planets were mislabeled, and the periodic table and moon phase diagrams contained nonsense entries including a "waning kreskin." parents have raised the errors with the school.

barriers close off much of the national mall for dc indycar race
large barrier walls have been erected across central washington, dc, blocking public access to much of the national mall during peak tourist season. the barriers are in place for an indycar race to be run through the city. residents and visitors have complained about the closures and restricted access to the monuments.

topics.snippet: The FBI released a tranche of several hundred internal documents related to the Epstein files search and redaction process over the past 24 hours. Among them is a spreadsheet listing flagged documents…
topics.text:
fbi documents show 16 epstein records flagged for "potus" reasons
the fbi released a tranche of several hundred internal documents related to the epstein files search and redaction process over the past 24 hours. among them is a spreadsheet listing flagged documents, 16 of which carry a marking reading "potus." the flagged items include phone message pads, magazines and newspaper articles. it is not clear why the documents were flagged or whether they have been released. the reporting is attributed to jason leopold at bloomberg.

topics.headline: Trump says he will not apologize for higher gas prices tied to Iran campaign
topics.snippet: Trump said he would never apologize for higher prices at the pump, telling Americans to remember when paying $4 a gallon that Iran will not have a nuclear weapon, and describing the increase as paying…
topics.text:
trump says he will not apologize for higher gas prices tied to iran campaign
trump said he would never apologize for higher prices at the pump, telling americans to remember when paying $4 a gallon that iran will not have a nuclear weapon, and describing the increase as paying "a tiny bit more" to defeat evil. he separately said the economy is performing well for wall street. the remarks come amid reporting that trump has privately discussed exiting the conflict without securing a deal on nuclear weapons.

topics.text:
trump crypto firm world liberty financial approved as federally chartered bank
a federal regulator approved the trump family crypto company world liberty financial to operate as a federally chartered bank. the institution's investors will not be disclosed and it will not be subject to fdic rules. critics say the arrangement allows undisclosed parties to funnel money into an entity owned by the president's family and raises the prospect of a future taxpayer-funded bailout.

topics.headline: Trump dismisses concerns over conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
topics.snippet: Responding to reports of poor conditions aboard ships deployed in the Middle East, Trump said military families are "not concerned" and that the deployment has "not gone on long enough," adding that t…
topics.text:
trump dismisses concerns over conditions aboard uss abraham lincoln
responding to reports of poor conditions aboard ships deployed in the middle east, trump said military families are "not concerned" and that the deployment has "not gone on long enough," adding that the ship is being moved shortly and replaced with a similar vessel. more than a dozen service members' families had raised concerns. historical comparison places the lincoln's reported 250-plus days at sea without a port call well outside the norm: vietnam-era carriers typically deployed six to nine months with port calls roughly monthly, and even in world war ii carriers rarely went more than 90 days between port visits.

navy weighs billions to redesign aircraft carriers to trump's preferred styling
washington post reporting indicates the navy is actively considering spending billions of dollars to redesign new aircraft carriers to match trump's aesthetic preferences, including a return to world war ii-era styling. the consideration comes as service members aboard carriers deployed in the middle east report poor living conditions and food quality.

topics.text:
karoline leavitt's abrupt resignation blindsides white house ahead of midterms
press secretary karoline leavitt's departure, scheduled for the end of the month, caught trump and the white house off guard, according to reporting from the independent. with the midterm elections roughly 80 days away, the white house has no plans to name a replacement and is scrambling over its communications strategy. the interim plan reportedly involves having vance, rubio, bessent and other officials brief reporters. her exit has also been linked to an incident in which staff remained aboard air force one during a reported assassination threat while trump departed separately.

bbc seeks subpoenas for kushner, ivanka trump and trump jr in defamation case
the bbc notified the court it intends to issue subpoenas to jared kushner, ivanka trump and donald trump jr, seeking communications from in and around january 6, 2021. the subpoenas are part of the $10 billion defamation lawsuit trump brought against the broadcaster. discovery has been largely stayed pending resolution of certain motions and an amendment to the complaint.

topics.text:
two mass shootings in 12 hours as us total reaches 297 this year
five people were killed and one injured in lake city, michigan, where the suspect was also killed. hours later, a shooting at virginia state university injured multiple people, with multiple suspects still at large and no life-threatening injuries reported. the two incidents bring the number of mass shootings in the united states this year to 297, exceeding the number of days elapsed in the year.

topics.text:
flock surveillance camera in austin found pointed at public pool
footage recorded by ben jordan shows a flock camera in austin, texas aimed directly at a public swimming pool rather than at roadways or license plates. the placement raises questions about whether the device is being used to surveil people at a public place. flock's chief executive has previously acknowledged that the company's cameras have been misused by law enforcement.

topics.text:
first patriot games close to sparse crowds amid criticism of politicization
the inaugural patriot games, staged as part of the country's 250th birthday celebrations, concluded with a few hundred people in the stands and organizers attempting to fill seats at the end. trump appeared on stage with the competitors. competitors did not necessarily represent the states they were listed under, including a texas participant competing for puerto rico, and the selection process was not made clear. cnn reported the field was predominantly white.

topics.headline: Trump's remarks about "young beautiful girls" at police event draw criticism
topics.snippet: Speaking before an audience of police officers, Trump repeatedly referred to "young beautiful girls" who visit the White House, recounting one who told him she had previously been afraid to leave her…
topics.text:
trump's remarks about "young beautiful girls" at police event draw criticism
speaking before an audience of police officers, trump repeatedly referred to "young beautiful girls" who visit the white house, recounting one who told him she had previously been afraid to leave her apartment and now walks to the white house each morning. officers were seen reacting awkwardly during the remarks. the comments drew confused responses online, including from some of his own supporters.

topics.headline: Sailors and families describe severe shortages aboard deployed warships as Hegseth disputes reports
topics.snippet: Family members and service members have described food shortages, lack of hygiene supplies and deteriorating living conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, with similar accounts now reported from t…
topics.text:
sailors and families describe severe shortages aboard deployed warships as hegseth disputes reports
family members and service members have described food shortages, lack of hygiene supplies and deteriorating living conditions aboard the uss abraham lincoln, with similar accounts now reported from the uss boxer, the uss bush and units in kuwait. cnn confirmed that one sailor went overboard from the lincoln last month, following military times reporting that sailors had sought to go overboard rather than continue an open-ended deployment. defense secretary pete hegseth said the accounts of deteriorating conditions had been "completely misrepresented." critics attribute the shortages to command decisions and the absence of a resupply plan, noting the ships have been at sea for extended periods with no available port.

topics.headline: Federal judge criticises Justice Department over Epstein files disclosures
topics.snippet: At a hearing at the federal courthouse in Washington, Judge Emmet Sullivan sharply criticised the Department of Justice for failing to explain why it had not properly redacted and released material re…
topics.text:
federal judge criticises justice department over epstein files disclosures
at a hearing at the federal courthouse in washington, judge emmet sullivan sharply criticised the department of justice for failing to explain why it had not properly redacted and released material required under the epstein files transparency act. department attorneys were described as unprepared and unable to provide new information to the court. an order from the judge is expected to follow.

topics.headline: Bulldozers move into Big Bend National Park for border wall construction
topics.snippet: The Department of Homeland Security waived environmental and historic preservation protections to allow border barrier construction inside Big Bend National Park in Texas, and heavy machinery has begu…
topics.text:
bulldozers move into big bend national park for border wall construction
the department of homeland security waived environmental and historic preservation protections to allow border barrier construction inside big bend national park in texas, and heavy machinery has begun work at the mouth of santa elena canyon. a $1.7 billion contract covers vehicle barriers, patrol roads, surveillance technology and possible lighting along the rio grande corridor. congress retains oversight and funding authority over the project and could require dhs and customs and border protection to release full plans.

topics.headline: Federal government posts record $432 billion July budget deficit
topics.snippet: The United States federal government recorded a $432.3 billion budget deficit for the month of July, the largest July deficit on record and the largest single-month shortfall since 2021. The figure ha…
topics.text:
federal government posts record $432 billion july budget deficit
the united states federal government recorded a $432.3 billion budget deficit for the month of july, the largest july deficit on record and the largest single-month shortfall since 2021. the figure has prompted criticism from within the republican party, with florida governor ron desantis calling it "the failure of doge in one sentence." the result has intensified internal disputes over fiscal policy ahead of 2028.

topics.headline: Records show federal surveillance of anti-ICE and anti-Flock activists
topics.snippet: Records reported by 404 Media indicate that government surveillance centres have monitored Instagram accounts opposed to Flock automated licence plate cameras and passed data to local law enforcement.…
topics.text:
records show federal surveillance of anti-ice and anti-flock activists
records reported by 404 media indicate that government surveillance centres have monitored instagram accounts opposed to flock automated licence plate cameras and passed data to local law enforcement. newly disclosed documents also describe a broader monitoring campaign targeting left-wing organisations, demonstrators and anti-ice activists, including infiltration of signal group chats and collection of financial records. critics argue the activity raises fourth amendment concerns.

topics.headline: US and Iran trade competing claims over control of the Strait of Hormuz
topics.snippet: Iran said it controls the Strait of Hormuz after President Trump claimed the United States had "total control" of the waterway. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US Navy can sustain its blockade…
topics.text:
us and iran trade competing claims over control of the strait of hormuz
iran said it controls the strait of hormuz after president trump claimed the united states had "total control" of the waterway. defense secretary pete hegseth said the us navy can sustain its blockade of iran indefinitely. the dispute comes amid continued disruption to shipping and fuel costs through the strait.

topics.headline: US has lost about 45 Reaper drones in the war with Iran
topics.snippet: The United States has lost roughly 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones during the war with Iran, amounting to about 25 percent of the Pentagon's Reaper fleet. The losses represent a substantial reduction in US long…
topics.text:
us has lost about 45 reaper drones in the war with iran
the united states has lost roughly 45 mq-9 reaper drones during the war with iran, amounting to about 25 percent of the pentagon's reaper fleet. the losses represent a substantial reduction in us long-endurance surveillance and strike capacity.

topics.headline: Hegseth's embrace of Christian nationalist adviser draws scrutiny at Pentagon
topics.snippet: Reporting by Mother Jones describes Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's adoption of teachings from his spiritual adviser Doug Wilson, a 73-year-old pastor and founder of Christ Church who advocates a pat…
topics.text:
hegseth's embrace of christian nationalist adviser draws scrutiny at pentagon
reporting by mother jones describes defense secretary pete hegseth's adoption of teachings from his spiritual adviser doug wilson, a 73-year-old pastor and founder of christ church who advocates a patriarchal society and what he calls biblical masculinity. critics say those views are being reflected in pentagon decisions during the war with iran, including blocking promotions for women, religious framing of strikes, and a focus on eliminating diversity programmes.

topics.headline: Israeli strikes in Lebanon and Gaza reported as fires spread
topics.snippet: Footage circulating shows incendiary devices launched into Lebanese territory, which posts describe as deliberately igniting wildfires, alongside reports of roughly 14 residential buildings bombed in…
topics.text:
israeli strikes in lebanon and gaza reported as fires spread
footage circulating shows incendiary devices launched into lebanese territory, which posts describe as deliberately igniting wildfires, alongside reports of roughly 14 residential buildings bombed in lebanon. separately, roads in gaza are being torn up, further limiting movement and access. the reports say mainstream outlets have not covered the incidents.

topics.headline: Gaza police chief killed in Israeli strike
topics.snippet: Jamal Abu Kamil, the police chief in Gaza, was killed when the vehicle he was driving was struck by multiple Israeli missiles. The strike was described as not survivable. Posts noted the absence of co…
topics.text:
gaza police chief killed in israeli strike
jamal abu kamil, the police chief in gaza, was killed when the vehicle he was driving was struck by multiple israeli missiles. the strike was described as not survivable. posts noted the absence of coverage from major broadcasters.

topics.headline: Document shows DOJ signed off on release of Trump from IRS claims
topics.snippet: A document identified as Trump versus the Internal Revenue Service, signed off by Trump's own Attorney General at the Department of Justice, releases, waives and forever discharges the president from…
topics.text:
document shows doj signed off on release of trump from irs claims
a document identified as trump versus the internal revenue service, signed off by trump's own attorney general at the department of justice, releases, waives and forever discharges the president from claims, counterclaims, causes of action and appeals connected to his dealings with the irs. critics describe the arrangement as the executive branch granting the president immunity in a matter involving himself.

topics.headline: Kennedy Center board votes to inscribe Trump's name despite court order
topics.snippet: The Kennedy Center's board of directors voted to add an inscription reading "restored and renovated by President Donald J. Trump" beneath the Kennedy Center name, and to rename the surrounding site th…
topics.text:
kennedy center board votes to inscribe trump's name despite court order
the kennedy center's board of directors voted to add an inscription reading "restored and renovated by president donald j. trump" beneath the kennedy center name, and to rename the surrounding site the president donald j. trump plaza. the board avoided formally renaming the institution, which was the subject of a court order barring a name change. legal observers say the move may still conflict with that order.

topics.headline: Utah documents contradict Trump's claims about access to Bears Ears
topics.snippet: A June memo from Utah's Public Lands Policy Coordinating Office told the Interior Department there was "current recreational access" to Bears Ears, naming the Peavine Corridor, open to off-road vehicl…
topics.text:
utah documents contradict trump's claims about access to bears ears
a june memo from utah's public lands policy coordinating office told the interior department there was "current recreational access" to bears ears, naming the peavine corridor, open to off-road vehicles, and rig canyon, used on a popular 40-mile backpacking loop. in july, president trump said in the oval office that visitors could not hunt, fish or virtually even walk on the utah monuments. the proclamations lifted the mineral withdrawal on those acres, reopening them to uranium claims and oil and gas leasing. advocates are calling for congress to grant bears ears and grand staircase permanent protection.

topics.headline: Trump orders Navy to abandon electromagnetic catapults for steam systems
topics.snippet: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump directed the Navy to remove the electromagnetic aircraft launch system from its carriers and return to steam catapults, a change Navy officials ha…
topics.text:
trump orders navy to abandon electromagnetic catapults for steam systems
the wall street journal reported that president trump directed the navy to remove the electromagnetic aircraft launch system from its carriers and return to steam catapults, a change navy officials have resisted for years. experts warn the conversion would cost billions of dollars, require extensive production time and reduce fleet readiness. senator mark kelly criticised the decision, saying trump should "stick to what he knows best."

topics.headline: NATO fighter shoots down unidentified drone over Latvia
topics.snippet: A NATO fighter jet shot down a drone of unknown origin over Latvia near the Russian border. The incident adds to a series of airspace violations in the Baltic region.
topics.text:
nato fighter shoots down unidentified drone over latvia
a nato fighter jet shot down a drone of unknown origin over latvia near the russian border. the incident adds to a series of airspace violations in the baltic region.

topics.text:
ukrainian drone operators overwhelmed us troops in german exercise
a major us army exercise in germany reportedly saw ukrainian drone operators overwhelm american troops, illustrating how effective drone warfare tactics developed in ukraine have become. the results have raised questions about us readiness for that form of combat.

a pentagon watchdog review documented mold, asbestos and collapsing ceilings at us bases in the pacific. the findings concern infrastructure conditions at facilities housing deployed personnel.

topics.text:
trump signs memorandum to expand us shipbuilding
president trump signed a national security presidential memorandum aimed at expanding commercial shipbuilding capacity, building a maritime workforce and revitalising the industry. the white house described the measure as restoring america's maritime dominance.

topics.headline: Lockheed Martin test-fires containerized Kodiak launcher
topics.snippet: Lockheed Martin completed the first live-fire test of its Kodiak containerized launcher at the Yakima Training Center in Washington state, firing a Reduced-Range Practice Rocket. Designed to resemble…
topics.text:
lockheed martin test-fires containerized kodiak launcher
lockheed martin completed the first live-fire test of its kodiak containerized launcher at the yakima training center in washington state, firing a reduced-range practice rocket. designed to resemble a standard shipping container, kodiak can carry up to 12 guided rockets from the gmlrs family and is compatible with other mlrs munitions including atacms and prsm. the company says the system can be deployed across air, ground and maritime platforms.

topics.headline: Whole Foods recalls dozens of prepared foods over salmonella risk
topics.snippet: Whole Foods has recalled around 40 prepared food products, including guacamole, salsa and pico de gallo, across more than a dozen states because of possible salmonella contamination. The recall stems…
topics.text:
whole foods recalls dozens of prepared foods over salmonella risk
whole foods has recalled around 40 prepared food products, including guacamole, salsa and pico de gallo, across more than a dozen states because of possible salmonella contamination. the recall stems from a nationwide salmonella outbreak linked to jalapeños. details of the affected products are listed on the fda's website.

topics.headline: Air Force accelerates reinstatement for members affected by COVID vaccine mandate
topics.snippet: The Air Force is speeding up the return process for some service members who were separated under the COVID-19 vaccine mandate. The change applies to Air Force and Space Force personnel.

the air force is speeding up the return process for some service members who were separated under the covid-19 vaccine mandate. the change applies to air force and space force personnel.

topics.headline: Congress demands answers over conditions aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
topics.snippet: Multiple members of Congress, including Senators Ruben Gallego and Richard Blumenthal, are demanding access to the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln and answers from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth…
topics.text:
congress demands answers over conditions aboard uss abraham lincoln
multiple members of congress, including senators ruben gallego and richard blumenthal, are demanding access to the aircraft carrier uss abraham lincoln and answers from defense secretary pete hegseth after reports of food shortages, non-operational toilets, moldy showers, missing hygiene supplies and irregular mail during a deployment supporting operations against iran. family members and sailors have described service members attempting to jump overboard, and more than 200 relatives confronted acting navy secretary hung cao at town hall meetings; a navy admiral acknowledged the deployment is affecting sailors' health after the service had said in april that reports of shortages were false. the carrier is nearing 250 days deployed with roughly 200 consecutive days without a genuine port call, a modern record, having touched land only in guam and in oman under restrictions. officials cited by the wall street journal say the uss george washington will be sent to relieve the lincoln, though no timeline has been given, and a member of the armed services committee says an investigation will be conducted.

topics.headline: Republican senators flooded with calls demanding an end to the war in Iran
topics.snippet: Republican senators are receiving a heavy volume of constituent calls from across the political spectrum demanding an end to the war in Iran, according to new reporting. Several senators, including al…
topics.text:
republican senators flooded with calls demanding an end to the war in iran
republican senators are receiving a heavy volume of constituent calls from across the political spectrum demanding an end to the war in iran, according to new reporting. several senators, including allies of the white house, are said to be frustrated and are pressing the administration for answers, with the treatment of service members deployed abroad adding to the pressure. the white house is described as seeking a way out of the conflict with 82 days remaining before the midterm elections.

topics.headline: CIA reportedly finds Israeli intelligence on Iranian plot against Trump was not credible
topics.snippet: The CIA is reported to have concluded that intelligence Israel passed to the United States in July, indicating Iran planned to assassinate President Trump during a visit to Turkey, was not credible. T…
topics.text:
cia reportedly finds israeli intelligence on iranian plot against trump was not credible
the cia is reported to have concluded that intelligence israel passed to the united states in july, indicating iran planned to assassinate president trump during a visit to turkey, was not credible. the reported threat led to a shutdown in turkey and a covert flight change that moved trump to britain. iranian state media has mocked the secret plane switch. the claims are attributed to reporting by the washington post, al jazeera and the hormuz report.

topics.headline: Treasury halts enforcement of Corporate Transparency Act and deletes ownership database
topics.snippet: The Treasury Department has decided it will no longer enforce the Corporate Transparency Act of 2021, which required companies to report their beneficial ownership structures to a non-public database…
topics.text:
treasury halts enforcement of corporate transparency act and deletes ownership database
the treasury department has decided it will no longer enforce the corporate transparency act of 2021, which required companies to report their beneficial ownership structures to a non-public database available to law enforcement. information already reported by u.s. individuals is being deleted and no new filings will be required. the law was passed to help investigators trace shell companies used for money laundering, tax fraud and terrorism financing.

topics.headline: Karoline Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary
topics.snippet: President Trump announced that White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt will leave her position at the end of the month, saying she has decided to step down to spend more time with her family. Lea…
topics.text:
karoline leavitt to step down as white house press secretary
president trump announced that white house press secretary karoline leavitt will leave her position at the end of the month, saying she has decided to step down to spend more time with her family. leavitt recently returned from maternity leave after the birth of her second child. no successor has been named. her departure follows other women leaving cabinet and senior administration posts.

topics.headline: Food recalls surge amid cuts to federal monitoring programs
topics.snippet: Dozens of food recalls have been issued since the start of the current administration, covering products including eggs, ground beef, infant formula, deli meats, dairy products, produce and prepared m…
topics.text:
food recalls surge amid cuts to federal monitoring programs
dozens of food recalls have been issued since the start of the current administration, covering products including eggs, ground beef, infant formula, deli meats, dairy products, produce and prepared meals. not all of the recalls remain in effect, and the fda lists each one individually. experts have attributed the higher-than-usual volume in part to cuts made to federal programs that monitor food safety and manage recalls.

topics.headline: Arkansas teenager sues state trooper over violent arrest
topics.snippet: Eighteen-year-old Elisa Hackett has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas State Police Trooper Moises Arilano, alleging he slammed her to the ground and punched her in the face during an encounter in which…
topics.text:
arkansas teenager sues state trooper over violent arrest
eighteen-year-old elisa hackett has filed a lawsuit against arkansas state police trooper moises arilano, alleging he slammed her to the ground and punched her in the face during an encounter in which she posed no threat. video of the incident has circulated publicly. the suit describes the conduct as beyond acceptable law enforcement behavior.

topics.snippet: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton was asked during a telephone town hall why he cheated on his wife and did not answer, pivoting away from the question. Paxton is running for the U.S. Senate in Texas…
topics.text:
ken paxton freezes when asked about infidelity at telephone town hall
texas attorney general ken paxton was asked during a telephone town hall why he cheated on his wife and did not answer, pivoting away from the question. paxton is running for the u.s. senate in texas against james talarico in the general election. his past conduct, including the infidelity, has featured in the campaign.

topics.headline: Mitch McConnell unseen publicly for two months
topics.snippet: Senator Mitch McConnell has not been seen publicly for 60 days since being admitted to George Washington University Hospital, and is now believed to be recovering at his home, where Capitol Police det…
topics.text:
mitch mcconnell unseen publicly for two months
senator mitch mcconnell has not been seen publicly for 60 days since being admitted to george washington university hospital, and is now believed to be recovering at his home, where capitol police detail vehicles remain parked outside and the shades are drawn. ally scott jennings has said the senator is recovering at home, but no video or public appearance has been released and his office has not provided details to media outlets. mcconnell has continued to collect his taxpayer-funded salary during the absence, and kentucky constituents have received no direct update on his condition.

topics.headline: Arctic exploration wells leave lasting tundra damage despite temporary-road permits
topics.snippet: Oil exploration in Alaska's National Petroleum Reserve is permitted on the basis that ice roads frozen across the tundra in winter melt in spring and leave no permanent trace, and the permitting agenc…
topics.text:
arctic exploration wells leave lasting tundra damage despite temporary-road permits
oil exploration in alaska's national petroleum reserve is permitted on the basis that ice roads frozen across the tundra in winter melt in spring and leave no permanent trace, and the permitting agency describes the impact as temporary. a survey of conocophillips exploration well sites along fish creek found flattened vegetation, sheared tussocks along ice road paths, and a roughly 20-foot structure set in permanent concrete. rules require snow to reach about six inches deep before activity begins, but the depth is averaged across the reserve while local topography varies considerably. six months ago a rig working the program tipped over near an iñupiaq village and spilled 4,000 gallons of diesel onto the tundra under a $200 million insurance policy.

topics.headline: FAA hires more than 2,000 video gamers to train as air traffic controllers

topics.text:
faa hires more than 2,000 video gamers to train as air traffic controllers
the federal aviation administration has hired more than 2,000 video gamers to train as air traffic controllers, reaching 94% of its hiring goal, with another 2,000 candidates in the pipeline. transportation secretary sean duffy said gaming develops skills such as focus, quick decision-making and multitasking, telling cbs news that much of what gamers do resembles controlling air traffic.

two soldiers killed in army apache crash near salado, texas
a u.s. army ah-64 apache helicopter from fort hood crashed near salado, texas, killing both soldiers on board. the crash sparked a large grass fire and prompted evacuations nearby. the crew members' identities are being withheld pending notification of next of kin, and the cause remains under investigation.

iran says strait of hormuz stays closed as trump touts naval blockade
iran said the strait of hormuz will remain closed unless the united states meets tehran's conditions. trump said the u.s. has total control of the strait, describing the american naval blockade as a "wall of steel" and saying iran has no navy, no air force, unpaid soldiers and a decimated irgc. he separately said iran faces either continued economic pressure or potentially harder u.s. strikes.
